text:
maria: Heads-up — prospect (regional bank) asked for detailed answers on encryption & key management for a contract review. Main asks: BYOK options, HSM support, key rotation/retention, exportability, and audit logs. Can we consolidate what to tell them?

bryan: Short answer: yes to BYOK and HSM for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can do CMEK via cloud KMS providers with agreed key policy. We use envelope encryption (DEK wrapped by KEK). KEKs can be cloud-managed (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or customer-hosted HSM (KMIP) for Private installs. :white_check_mark:

tara: For POC scope, recommend we propose: 1) customer provide test KMS ARN / key-id + granting service account/role with kms:GenerateDataKey/kms:Decrypt/kms:Encrypt; 2) we run a short smoke test generating DEKs and encrypting a sample artifact; 3) verify audit events (CloudTrail / Audit Logs) are visible to customer.

sam: Quick Q — do we ever request exportable key material? Prospect specifically asked if Redwood will ever need the raw key.

bryan: No. We never request or store raw KEK material. For cloud KMS: KEKs are non-exportable by default. For BYOK where customer imports key material into a cloud KMS, exportability depends on the KMS; but Redwood never asks to export KEK. For Private with customer HSM, keys stay in their appliance.

kevin-cust: Confirming: if we rotate our KMS key, will Redwood lose the ability to decrypt past artifacts (e.g., cached model contexts)? What's the recommended rotation pattern?

bryan: Important nuance — we use DEKs (data encryption keys) to encrypt persisted blobs; DEKs are wrapped by your KEK. If you rotate the KEK, decryption of existing wrapped-DEKs succeeds as long as the KMS still allows Decrypt with the older key version or you keep the old key material available. Cloud KMS typically keeps key versions accessible unless you schedule a permanent deletion. Recommended pattern: rotate KEK on your cadence (e.g., 90 days) but keep prior key versions for a retention window (30–90 days) to ensure decryption of in-flight/archived DEKs, or proactively rewrap DEKs during maintenance.

tara: For the POC/contract we should call out: "Redwood supports customer-managed KEKs; customer is responsible for rotation policy and retaining key versions needed for decrypting previously-wrapped DEKs." We can offer professional-services assistance to rewrap objects during cutover.

sam: What about HSM specifics — do we support FIPS/HSM-backed keys for compliance posture?

bryan: Yes. On cloud: AWS KMS keys are HSM-backed (FIPS 140-2 level depends on region/service) and we can require HSM-backed keys in your KMS policy. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs over KMIP or with an HSM appliance in the same network. We also support attestation artifacts from KMS (e.g., AWS KMS key attestation) on request for due diligence.

maria: Can we drop an example IAM role policy snippet for their security team to speed approvals?

bryan: Sure — minimal permissions we need for the smoke test / POC:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE-KEY-ID"
    }
  ]
}
```

bryan: Also note: for production we ask for least-privilege roles with an assume-role pattern from Redwood's service account. We'll share exact principal once the SOW is signed.

kevin-cust: Audit logs — we need proof that Redwood's KMS usage is logged. Where do those appear? Can we get an export?

bryan: All KMS API calls made by Redwood are visible in the customer's CloudTrail / Audit Logs (for cloud KMS). We can provide guidance on log retention and can also send our own operational logs (redact PII) to a customer-approved S3/GCS destination if agreed in the contract. For Private, logs are in your environment and you control retention.

tara: One more edge: exportability & BYOK import methods. If the customer wants to import raw key material into AWS KMS (ImportKeyMaterial), that's supported but once imported keys are marked non-exportable by KMS. If they want fully externalizable key material and Redwood to use it, they'd need Private deployment where the HSM exposes keys via KMIP and allows Redwood to call the HSM over your network.

sam: Anything legal/security wants called out for the contract?

bryan: Call out: 1) Redwood will not store or export KEK material; 2) customer retains responsibility for KEK rotation and retention of previous versions for decrypting historical artifacts; 3) for Hosted/CMEK we need a key policy that allows Redwood's service principal to call GenerateDataKey/Decrypt — we can provide exact text; 4) attestation/audit docs available on request (SOC2 report, KMS attestation).

maria: I'll draft answers and the POC checklist for the AE bundle. Quick POC checklist for sales slide (single-line items): 1) Provide test KMS key-id + role; 2) Grant minimal KMS perms; 3) Redwood runs encrypt/decrypt smoke test; 4) Verify CloudTrail events and sample audit export; 5) Optional: HSM attestation for compliance; 6) Confirm rotation/retention plan.

deploy-bot: Deployed artifact: sales/poс-crypto-checklist v1 -> shared with prospect (link: https://redwood.internal/sales/poс-crypto-checklist). :rocket:

kevin-cust: Thanks — that helps. We'll prepare the test key + role and ping you early next week.

maria: Perfect — tagging @bryan and @tara for any final comments before I send the SOW language. :thumbsup:
